parole.significato: bow; bowknot, ribbon (long, narrow strip of material)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Band. Further from Proto-Germanic *bandiz. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰendʰ-.
Borrowed from German Gruppe. Omitting several steps, from Proto-Germanic *kruppaz. Doublet of круп (krup) and крупье́ (krupʹjé).
Borrowed from German Krengel, variant of Kringel.

parole.significato: lapel (at the end of a sleeve), cuff
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Aufschlag. Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *slahaną (whence English slay, slag). Doublet of аншла́г (anšlág), дуршла́г (duršlág), форшла́г (foršlág), шлаг (šlag), and шлагба́ум (šlagbáum) and more distantly doublet of шлак (šlak) and шля́хта (šljáxta).
Borrowed from German Pfäulein, a diminutive of Pfau from Old High German pāwo, from Proto-Germanic *pāwô, itself a borrowing from Latin pāvō.

Borrowed from German fechten + -овать (-ovatʹ). Further from Proto-Germanic *fehtaną (whence also English fight). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *peḱ-. Borrowed from German Spion. Omitting several steps, from Proto-Germanic *spehōną, further from Proto-Indo-European *speḱ-. Root cognate (via PIE) with Latin speculātor, Ancient Greek κατάσκοπος (katáskopos). Compare typologically согляда́тай (sogljadátaj) (akin to гляде́ть (gljadétʹ)).
